rationale: A wins because it knows the difference between a tension and a trend. “The app that made women message first will now help write the message” is tight, reportable, and drawn from the facts; B’s “Dating apps are selling AI to users who say AI ruins dating” turns one Bumble relaunch and “some users” into a category claim it cannot cash. B has sharper proof questions in places, but it let one shiny unsupported angle onto the list, and that is how founders end up pitching vibes.
gaps_in_A: “The relaunch is the founder's first big public move since returning as CEO this year” is not in the update. Maybe true, maybe not; prove it or drop “first.”
“Bumble's entire brand is a single authentic human gesture” overstates the supplied fact. The update says women-message-first remains core, not that the entire brand reduces to one gesture.

The product proof stops at “whether the AI helps write the woman's first message specifically.” It should also demand whether the tool drafts, rewrites, suggests, sends, defaults on, and discloses AI assistance to the recipient.
“Story type: funding-mechanics” is the wrong label for a public-company user/stock story. Small thing, but sloppy taxonomy is still slop.
gaps_in_B: “Dating apps are selling AI to users who say AI ruins dating” is the bad overreach. The facts give Bumble, singular, and “some users” calling AI in dating inauthentic, not a category of apps or users saying AI ruins dating.

“Bumble is a usable anchor rather than the whole story” admits the problem while keeping the angle anyway. Without comparable moves by other dating apps, this should be conditional or refused, not pitched as trend.
“it is the first substantive product move since the founder's return this year” is not supplied. Same founder-return frame works without inventing primacy.

“the company has made a claim the next disclosure will settle” overstates the record. The update says the relaunch follows user and stock declines; it does not say Bumble claimed the next paying-user disclosure will prove the relaunch.
